title: Cosh_G(X,R,φ)[Σ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_φ(G) (§3 Cor)
body_html:
Localization equivalence

Corollary. Suppose the counit $H_0(C_\bullet(\Loc_\phi V)) \to V$ of the adjunction [[node:representations.h0_C_dot_adjoint]] is an isomorphism for every $V \in \Rep_\phi(G)$. Then the induced functor $$H_0 \circ C_\bullet \;:\; \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)[\Sigma^{-1}] \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \Rep_\phi(G)$$ is an equivalence, where $\Sigma$ is the class of morphisms $\alpha$ in $\Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ for which $H_0 \circ C_\bullet(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism.
proof_html:
This is [Gabriel–Zisman, §1.3] applied to the adjunction. The quasi-inverse is induced by $\Loc_\phi$. $\square$

This corollary is the schematic model for the fully fledged equivalence $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)[E_\Phi^{-1}] \simeq \Rep_\Phi(G)$ proved in §7.4 once the counit-isomorphism hypothesis is verified via the resolution theorem Resolution theorem: C_•(Φ, V) → V (Thm 7.1.7).
